title: Diel variations in stream chemistry and isotopic composition of dissolved inorganic carbon, upper Clark Fork River, Montana, USA
water_body: Upper Clark Fork River, sites AS1 and AS2 (2.5 h travel time apart), near Deer Lodge, Montana; 31 Jul-1 Aug 2003
location_in_paper: Results text: 'Concentrations of dissolved Mn and Zn at both sites increased during the night by 100% and 500%, respectively (Fig. 4)'; Results text: 'The diel change in pH at both sites was approximately 0.5 pH units'; Discussion: pH increased from approximately 8.2 to 8.7 (calcite discussion)
notes: Computed: 500% night-time increase -> C_night/C_day = 6.0; slope = log10(6.0)/(8.2-8.7). Same amplitude reported for both sites, so one row. Extremes not given as simultaneous clock times; text says metals rose at night and fell by day, and abstract says the changes 'were positively correlated to diel changes in pH, dissolved O2, and water temperature' (wording ambiguous; concentration-pH relation implied inverse). Temperature co-varied (8 C), so slope is pH+T combined. DO 65% to >150% saturation. Authors favour biofilm-mediated daytime oxidative precipitation of Fe/Mn oxides and night-time reductive dissolution over simple pH sorption, because particulate Mn and Zn also rose at night; calcite co-precipitation also considered.

title: The influence of hydrous Mn-Zn oxides on diel cycling of Zn in an alkaline stream draining abandoned mine lands
water_body: High Ore Creek water (1 L) + 20 g natural hydrous Mn-Zn oxide (HMZO) crust from the creek; pH set by CO2/air bubbling
location_in_paper: Text, Series 4 and 5 HMZO experiments and Fig. 9: 'linear regression of the combined data (Fig. 9) yielded slopes of 0.90 for Zn (r2 = 0.91) and 1.04 for Mn (r2 = 0.94)'; equations log Zn = -0.899pH + 6.532 (r2 = 0.911), log Mn = -1.040pH + 6.299 (r2 = 0.935)
notes: Design is experimental_pH, not diel: lab test within a diel study, included because it isolates pH from temperature for the same sorbent that drives the field cycle. Sign converted to the d log10(C)/d pH convention (authors quote slope magnitude 0.90). Metals equilibrated within hours of each pH change; Zn:Mn mass ratio ~20:1. Temperature dependence (separate test at pH 8.15 +/- 0.05, 6-22 C): Zn and Mn decreased ~2.5-fold as T rose (2.4-fold for 5 to 20 C in abstract), r2 = 0.95 (Zn) and 0.86 (Mn) vs 1/T; adsorption enthalpies +50.3 (Zn) and +46.0 (Mn) kJ/mol. Authors: field diel Zn in High Ore Creek is better predicted using both pH and T than pH alone.
